definitions.explanation: A seven-day period centered on the spring or autumn equinox, during which Japanese families visit graves and make offerings to ancestors. One of the most important Buddhist observances in Japan.

definitions.gloss: the other shore, the far bank; nirvana
definitions.explanation: In Buddhist philosophy, the realm of enlightenment on the other side of the river of suffering. The opposite of 此岸 (this shore, the world of earthly suffering).

examples.japanese: {彼岸|ひがん}にお{墓参|はかまい}りをする。
examples.english: We visit graves during the equinox.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}の{彼岸|ひがん}にはぼたもちを{作|つく}る。
examples.english: We make botamochi during the spring equinox.

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}さ{寒|さむ}さも{彼岸|ひがん}まで。
examples.english: Both heat and cold last only until the equinox.
examples.notes: A well-known proverb meaning extreme weather moderates around the equinox.

examples.english: To cross to the other shore (to attain enlightenment).

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}では、{苦|く}しみの{世界|せかい}を{此岸|しがん}、{悟|さと}りの{世界|せかい}を{彼岸|ひがん}と{呼|よ}ぶ。
examples.english: In Buddhism, the world of suffering is called 'this shore' and the world of enlightenment is called 'the other shore.'

examples.japanese: {修行|しゅぎょう}を{重|かさ}ね、ついに{彼岸|ひがん}に{至|いた}った。
examples.english: After years of training, he finally reached the other shore.

notes:
SENSE 1 (equinox period):
The {彼岸|ひがん} period lasts seven days: the equinox day itself, three days before, and three days after. There are two per year:
- {春|はる}の{彼岸|ひがん}: spring equinox (around March 20-21)
- {秋|あき}の{彼岸|ひがん}: autumn equinox (around September 22-23)

Traditional foods:
- ぼたもち: rice balls with sweet bean paste (spring)
- おはぎ: similar to ぼたもchi but named differently (autumn)

PROVERB:
{暑|あつ}さ{寒|さむ}さも{彼岸|ひがん}まで: Both heat and cold end by the equinox.

SENSE 2 (the other shore):
From Sanskrit pāramitā ({波羅蜜多|はらみった}). The Buddhist concept contrasts {此岸|しがん} (this shore, the world of suffering) with {彼岸|ひがん} (the other shore, nirvana). The equinox observance (sense 1) derives from this concept.
